There was an interesting article in The Economist last week on a what-if scenario about countries sending rockets to nudge a potentially deadly asteroid away from colliding with earth. Apparently there is a real risk, under international law, that if you interfered with it it would go from being a "celestial body", for which nobody is responsible, to being a "space object" for which you are now responsible if it then does hit something.
And then nobody would do anything because they wouldn't want to take the blame for it.

That was sort of the point of the piece, in that it is much more complicated than you might think, not just from a technical perspective but also from a liability for unintended consequences perspective. I expect the same would hold if you started messing about with the ocean currents or tried to fix the earth's climate. Even if the overall result for the world was positive someone would almost certainly be worse off and they would sue the hell out of you. Link although it might be behind a paywall
